summary: Alexander Eggers was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Tartu (1885–1894), studying under Leo Meyer and Leopold von Schroeder. He later served at Tallinn Cathedral School (1896–1914) and Privatlyzeum Greifswald (1919–1928).
Alexander Faulkner worked in Indology and government service. He served in the Indian Civil Service in 1839 and was Assistant Commissioner in the Customs, Salt, and Opium Department until 1874.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (c. 1903–1907) and Christian Bartholomae (c. 1907–1908).

Alexander Gardner works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., also studying under Robert H. Sharf and Janet Gyatso, and held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Alexander Hamilton was an Indologist who taught scholars such as Franz Bopp and Friedrich Schlegel. He served as Professor at the East India Company College (1806–1818) and founded the Royal Asiatic Society in 1823.
Alexander Henderson Diack was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Aberdeen (1876–1879) and King's College, Cambridge (1879–1881).
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued PhD studies at the University of Toronto and held a post as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied law at Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Chief Justice of Ceylon (c. 1811–1819) and co-founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1823.

Alexander Kabanoff worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Around 2000, he was a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at Kazan Imperial University (c. 1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (c. 1849–1870).

Alexander Kingsbury Smith specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having earned an MPhil from Oxford and a PhD from EPHE. He has taught at EPHE and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and founded Armchair Academics and Ligature Historical Filmwerke.

Alexander Kinloch Forbes was an Indologist and historian who studied at the East India Company College and under Dalpatram. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1862) and founded the Gujarat Vernacular Society and Forbes Gujarati Sabha.

Alexander Lubotsky is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, becoming Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).

Alexander Meyrick Broadley was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied law at Lincoln's Inn (c. 1866–1869) and served in the Indian Civil Service as an Assistant and Collector (1869–1872).
Alexander Murray was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Edinburgh (c. 1794–1812), where he was appointed Professor of Oriental Languages in 1812.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in religious and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer. He held a teaching position at North Dakota State University (c. 2018–2019).

Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at Moscow State University. He held positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and SOAS University of London, where he was Professor from 1990 to 2001.

Alexander Potebnja worked in linguistics and philosophy, completing his doctorate at the University of Kharkiv and studying under Albrecht Weber. He served as a professor at the University of Kharkiv from 1875 until 1891.

Alexander Rea was an archaeologist and Indologist who spent his career at the Archaeological Survey of India, joining as an Assistant in 1882, becoming head in 1886, and serving as Superintendent from 1902 to 1913.
